aperture_validity.basis: the source marks surface 7 as the aperture stop, and that same row carries 0.30 mm of glass (nd 1.52113): the stop is the clear aperture of that refracting surface, the plane front face of a plane-parallel plate. The row's clear semi-diameter (0.25 mm, a derived nominal opening) is smaller than the plate's edged outline (0.52 mm), so light outside the opening meets the plate's opaque rim
aperture_validity.consequence: the opening limits the beam, so the record is eligible for stop-dependent evaluation; the engine carries the stop as that surface's clear aperture and builds no separate plate (conversion counts report aperture_stops 0)
aperture_validity.satisfaction_basis: eligibility only: a stop-dependent match needs evidence (a field point or pupil sample), which this batch does not assert

spectrum.sampling_wavelengths_basis: SOURCE_STATED air wavelength 587.5618 nm (the d line), converted once to vacuum with the engine's own air model (6432.8 / 2949810 / 25540, material_physics.air_index_exact) to 587.7218645 nm. The table states no column label for its index column, but its values reproduce published d-line pairs exactly (1.88300 / 40.76 = N-LASF31A, 1.92286 / 18.90 = H-ZF72A, 1.72916 / 54.68 = H-LAK52, 1.51633 / 64.14 = S-BSL7), so the table is read as d-line data
spectrum.wavelength_precision: full precision as used by the Project; rounded values in this document are for display only

sampling_span_nm.note: the source states one index per glass at the d line. A zero-width interval cannot be filtered, so the span is a +/-0.5 nm window around that one sample; it is a numerical convenience, not a second wavelength and not a measured band

continuous_coverage_nm.note: the source states no operating wavelength range; a single d-line index per glass does not establish continuous coverage

effective_focal_length_mm.definition: Signed paraxial effective focal length of the native Project.

back_focal_length_mm.definition: Signed paraxial distance from the last optical surface vertex to the rear focal point for collimated input.

total_track_mm.definition: Axial distance from the first optical surface to the image plane.

engine_check.method: thick-lens paraxial ABCD through the committed Project's COMPOUND unit

comparison.rule: per quantity: |engine - source| <= atol + rtol * scale, with scale = |EFL| for the effective focal length and max(|BFL|, |EFL|) for the back focal length. atol = 0.005 mm is half a unit in the last decimal of the coarsest focal length these publications print (two decimals); rtol = 2e-3 is 1e-3 for a prescription printed to four decimals on radii as small as 0.27 mm plus 1e-3 for the engine's air-referenced index convention

effective_focal_length.basis: the source states no such first-order value

back_focal_length.basis: the source states no such first-order value

comparison.why: the publication states neither an effective focal length nor a back focal length for this example, so the two-quantity rule has no pair to judge. The engine's values are recorded under engine_check as ENGINE_COMPUTED facts and no verdict is claimed

engine_check.note: the engine's back focal length is the component's infinite-conjugate value: the paraxial focus of an object at infinity lies 0.0367 mm before the last surface vertex. The design's own conjugate is finite (36.0000 mm object distance); for that conjugate the same ABCD puts the focus at z = 6.93146 mm, 0.0051 mm behind the source's stated image plane at z = 6.9264 mm

nominal_effective_focal_length_mm.note: this batch's brief carries no parameter table for US8715170B2, so the source states no effective focal length; no source value exists to compare against

nominal_back_focal_length_mm.definition: from the last surface vertex to the paraxial image point, positive downstream

aperture.note: the source's prescription table states no F-number, no entrance pupil diameter and no numerical aperture, and this batch's brief carries no parameter table for the publication, so no system-aperture value is asserted rather than inferred

clear_semi_diameter_mm.note: the source states no clear aperture. The opening was set to 0.25 mm as a nominal endoscope pupil (about f/3.0 at the engine's 1.5201 mm focal length); it is a conversion choice, not a source value, and it changes no first-order quantity

approximations.detail: every glass is a constant index at the source's stated nd; the source's vd is recorded but no dispersion curve is modelled, so axial colour and chromatic focal shift are not represented
the Project is evaluated at the d line only

the source states no clear apertures, no F-number and no field, so the rule EFL/(2*F#) cannot be applied. Semi-diameters are nominal: the stop opening was set to 0.25 mm and every other surface was given a clear semi-diameter large enough for the axial beam of that opening (the marginal ray reaches at most 0.46 mm, at surface 11) and growing toward the image side in three steps (0.50 mm on the front window and the two front elements, 0.55 mm after the stop, 0.58 mm on the cemented doublet, 0.70 mm on the final plane-parallel stack), each edged at 0.02 mm beyond the clear aperture. They set the stop plate and the solid checks, not the first-order values

the source's stop is surface 7, and that row carries 0.30 mm of glass (nd 1.52113) rather than an air gap, so the stop cannot be a separate plate: it is carried as surface 7's clear aperture (the opening) inside a refracting surface. The opening is preserved and the plate's rim outside it blocks light, but the stop is not a member of its own (conversion counts report aperture_stops 0)

the source's object-surface row states 36.0000 mm, read as the object distance (the distance from the object plane to surface 1). The engine's paraxial focus for that conjugate lands at z = 6.93146 mm against the stated image plane at z = 6.9264 mm, 0.0051 mm apart, which supports the reading; the record keeps the object at 36 mm rather than at infinity
nominal prescription surfaces; no figure, centring or surface-roughness error is modelled

wavelength_band_nm.basis: the intersection of the valid bands of the materials used

conversion.surface_labels: the source's own surface numbers are kept as the row labels, except the stop: source surface 7 is labelled STO (the importer's stop label). Surfaces 1-2 (0.45 mm window), 3-4, 5-6, 7-8 (the stop plate), 9-10, 11-13 (cemented doublet) and 14-17 (cemented plane-parallel stack) are the source's own groups; no surface was added, removed or renumbered
